limitations: Java waterlogged is candidate evidence, not proof of Bedrock or NEMC support.
Absence of Java waterlogged is not proof that a Bedrock block cannot coexist with water.
Exact UIBI joins can include downgraded target blocks; inspect universal/Java/Bedrock names before testing.
The Bedrock converter maps foreground state only; wet/dry universal states may collapse to the same Bedrock output.
Evidence includes at most two wet and two dry examples per name; counts include all converter output records.
Native registry name presence does not prove the mapped semantic state is available or waterloggable.

purpose: offline candidate discovery for NEMC native placement verification; not a runtime capability allowlist
